description:
One source to record, written as its own group in the file.

Fill it by dragging a stream onto it — from the Available list
in the recorder window, or from the service tree here — by
double-clicking one in the Available list, or by typing an
address:  discover:///?stream=NAME&name=SERVICE

Click 'keep' / 'once' to set what happens if the producing
service stops:
keep — wait and reconnect by service + stream name, continuing
      into the same file and the same dataset. A restarted or
      reconfigured amplifier is still recognised. The default.
once — do not reconnect; the stream ends for good.

Click the name for details and to copy the address.
Click ✕ to clear the slot.
label: Stream 3
name: stream3

description:
gzip level applied to the data as it is written to the file.

0 = off (default). Written raw, at full speed; the file grows at
      about the data rate shown per stream.
1 = fastest, least saving.
6 = a good balance — close to 9's saving for a fraction of the CPU.
9 = maximum saving, most CPU.

How much it saves depends on the signal, not on the level: a
synthetic test sine compresses about 24x, real EEG nearer 2x. The
cost is paid on the recording path, at every sample, which is why
off is the default.

Nothing is lost. gzip is lossless and a compressed file opens in
any HDF5 tool with no extra steps.

Applies to the NEXT file — a dataset's compression is fixed when it
is created, so changing this mid-recording does not affect the file
in progress.
label: Compression (0 = off)
name: compression

description:
How often data already received is committed to the file.

This bounds what a crash or a power loss costs: at the default of
2 s you lose at most the last two seconds. Everything before the
last flush stays readable even if the machine dies mid-recording.

Lower is safer and costs a little more I/O; higher batches writes.
There is little reason to move far from the default unless a slow
disk is struggling.

Range 1–600 s.
label: Flush to disk every [s]
name: flushSeconds

description:
Show the recorder's own window: the slots, the live per-stream
rates, and the list of available streams.

Turning it off leaves the recorder running with only the tray icon
and the status strip, which is what an unattended rig wants.
Middle-click the tray icon to bring the window back.
label: Show window
name: showUi

description:
How many stream slots exist — how many sources can be recorded.

Raising it adds empty slots at the end; lowering it removes slots
from the end. To clear a slot in the middle, use the ✕ next to it.

While recording this cannot go below the number of slots that
existed when the file was opened: the file's datasets were created
from them, and removing a slot would only hide something that is
still being written. Raising it still works.
label: Number of streams
name: streamsCount

description:
Mark the moment something happened, with a line of text —
"bad trial", "subject moved".

The timestamp is taken when the box OPENS, not when you press Mark,
so you can react immediately and take as long as you like over the
wording.

The note is written into the file being recorded and published on
the recorder's 'annotations' stream. With no recording running it
still goes out on the stream, but has no file to land in.

Same box as a double-click on the tray icon, or the Note… button in
the recorder window.
label: Annotation
name: annotate

description:
Begin recording about two seconds after the service starts, with no
operator present. For unattended rigs.

The delay lets discovery find the configured sources first — without
it a recording opens with every slot in 'waiting', which looks like
a fault.

Off: recording starts only when someone presses Record, or a client
sends the 'start' transition.
label: Start rec on launch
name: autoStart

description:
Name of the HDF5 file to write.

A run of $ is replaced by a run number that counts up, so a session
is never overwritten: record-$$$$.h5 becomes record-0001.h5, then
record-0002.h5, and so on.

A bare name goes to the recording folder (RESONANCE_RECORD_PATH,
set by env.bat to <distribution>\data). An absolute path is used
exactly as given.

Locked while recording — the name is read when the file is opened.
label: File name
name: fileName

description:
Show the small always-on-top bar above the taskbar: a state dot,
the file size, elapsed time and the combined data rate.

Drag it anywhere. Double-click it to add a note; middle-click it to
bring the recorder window to the front.

The dot is grey when idle, green while recording, and red when a
stream has dropped.
label: Show status strip
name: showStrip
